title: Semantic Layer
body: A centralized data abstraction layer that defines business metrics and entities once, then serves them consistently to BI tools, analytics dashboards, and AI/ML applications. Prevents metric proliferation and conflicting definitions across teams.

title: Headless BI / Headless Analytics
body: An architecture where the semantic layer is decoupled from the visualization/presentation layer. Metrics are defined centrally and consumed by multiple frontends (Power BI, Tableau, GenAI agents, REST APIs) without each one defining logic independently.

title: Metric Definition / Metric Store
body: A centralized repository of business metrics (e.g., 'Monthly Active Users', 'Net Premium Earned') that includes the SQL logic, dimensions, filters, and business rules. Once defined, metrics are reused across all analytics tools.

title: Cube.dev
body: An open-source semantic layer and headless BI platform. Sits between data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery) and frontends (Tableau, Grafana, custom apps). Handles metric definitions, role-based access, and provides REST/GraphQL APIs.

title: dbt Semantic Layer / MetricFlow
body: dbt's native semantic layer (formerly MetricFlow) that lives in dbt projects. Enables centralized metric definitions using YAML, automatic SQL generation, and integration with dbt Cloud. Metrics are queryable via dbt APIs and BI tools.

title: Metric Definition YAML (dbt)
body: YAML syntax used in dbt projects to define business metrics centrally. Includes metric name, type (simple, derived), SQL templates, dimensions, filters, and description. Enables one-time definition, multi-tool consumption.

title: Metric Consumption / Metric API
body: Downstream applications (BI tools, dashboards, GenAI agents) query metrics through APIs (REST, GraphQL, JDBC) rather than direct SQL. Ensures metric definitions are applied consistently and audit trails are maintained.

title: Metric Federation
body: Technique for combining metrics across multiple data sources (different databases, clouds, teams) into a unified semantic layer. Enables consistent metric definitions even when underlying data is distributed.

title: Dimension
body: In semantic layers and BI, a dimension is a categorical attribute used to slice and dice metrics. Examples: Product Category, Region, Customer Segment, Time Period. Dimensions enable drill-down analysis from aggregate metrics.

title: Fact Table
body: A table in a data warehouse containing quantitative measurements (facts) along with foreign keys to dimension tables. Example: A 'Sales Fact' table with columns like transaction_id, amount, timestamp, and foreign keys to customer, product, store dimensions.

metadata.source: Data Warehouse Design Standards, Kimball Methodology

title: Power BI Semantic Model
body: Microsoft Power BI's equivalent of a semantic layer. Defines relationships, hierarchies, calculations (DAX measures), and role-based security. Power BI reports consume this model rather than querying raw tables directly.

title: DAX (Data Analysis Expressions)
body: Microsoft's formula language for Power BI and Excel. Used to define calculated columns, measures, and KPIs. DAX syntax enables complex aggregations, time-intelligence functions, and row-context calculations.

title: Tableau Data Model / Live Connection
body: Tableau's approach to connecting semantic layers. Can use live connections (direct query to semantic layer) or extracted data (periodic syncs). Tableau Desktop users build visualizations without writing SQL if the semantic layer is well-defined.

title: KPI (Key Performance Indicator)
body: A quantifiable measure used to track business performance (e.g., Customer Acquisition Cost, Net Premium Income, Claims Loss Ratio). KPIs are high-level metrics tied directly to business objectives and typically monitored at C-suite level.

title: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) in Semantic Layer
body: Security model where users are assigned roles, and each role has defined permissions to view/query specific dimensions, metrics, or rows. Semantic layers enforce RBAC to ensure users see only authorized data.

title: Star Schema
body: A database design pattern used in data warehouses with a central fact table surrounded by dimension tables. Optimized for analytical queries (OLAP), enabling fast aggregations along multiple dimensions.

title: Snowflake Schema
body: A variation of star schema where dimension tables are normalized into multiple related tables. Reduces data redundancy but adds complexity to queries. Less common than star schema in modern semantic layers.

title: Mart / Data Mart
body: A subset of a data warehouse focused on a specific business domain or team (e.g., Sales Mart, Claims Mart). Data marts are often built from the central warehouse and optimized for specific analytical use cases.

title: Hub-and-Spoke Analytics Model
body: Organizational model where a central architecture team (hub) defines standards, governance, and reusable components, while business teams (spokes) build solutions using the hub's frameworks. Wawanesa's P&C and Life teams are spokes consuming hub semantic definitions.

metadata.source: Enterprise Architecture Patterns, Wawanesa Job Description

title: Guardrails (in Analytics)
body: Pre-built policies, templates, and constraints enforced by the hub to ensure spoke teams comply with governance standards. Examples: enforced PII masking, mandatory row-level security on customer data, approved metric definitions.

title: Metric Drift / Metric Definition Drift
body: When different teams inadvertently create conflicting definitions of the same business metric (e.g., two versions of 'Revenue' with different calculation rules). A centralized semantic layer prevents this.

title: Single Source of Truth (SSOT)
body: A governance principle where each piece of data/metric is defined and maintained in exactly one place. Enables consistency, auditability, and prevents duplicate work. Semantic layers enforce SSOT for metrics.

title: Data Lineage
body: The ability to trace data from its source through transformations to final consumption. Semantic layers track lineage from raw data → transformations → metrics → dashboards, enabling impact analysis and debugging.

title: GraphQL API for Metrics
body: A query language and API standard used by some semantic layers (Cube, Apollo) to enable flexible metric queries. Clients can request exactly the dimensions and metrics needed, reducing over-fetching of data.

title: REST API for Metrics
body: RESTful endpoints that allow applications to query metrics from a semantic layer using standard HTTP methods. Enables integration with dashboards, LLMs, and custom applications without direct SQL access.

title: Metric Aggregation
body: Process of combining raw data points into summary statistics (sum, average, count) along dimensions. Semantic layers handle aggregation definitions to ensure consistent roll-up logic across all consumers.

title: Slowly Changing Dimension (SCD)
body: A technique for handling dimensional data that changes over time (e.g., customer regions, product categories). SCD Types (0-4) define strategies for preserving historical dimension values while tracking changes.
